audit.whatIsWrong: The content-layer level chart gave Cassiopeia all seven stages while the full layer gave Xerath all seven, the page rates the matchup HARD 8/10, and the win rate is 46.59% over 792 games.
audit.why: Xerath outranges every Cassiopeia tool at every stage: Arcanopulse 750, Eye of Destruction 1000, Shocking Orb 1050, Rite of the Arcane 5000, against Cassiopeia's 850 Q and 700 E. The full layer and the win rate agree; the content chart was the outlier and packet.defects flags it.
audit.corrected: win[0..6] flipped to Xerath with whys[0..6] rewritten to match, and the full-layer phases[N].why rewritten so each row's sentence agrees with its 'Xerath' side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every phases[N].why was the generic Cassiopeia template describing her winning the stage, under a side that said Xerath.
audit.why: The row and the sentence under it argued with each other on all seven rows.
audit.corrected: All seven whys rewritten around Xerath's ranges and cooldowns and Cassiopeia's Seraph's spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rite of the Arcane (R) is a channel and Petrifying Gaze cancels it — never stated. The content layer also invented an ability name, 'Mage Chains', for Xerath's E.
audit.why: brief.missingInteractions carries channel-interruptible; the kit names the E Shocking Orb. 'Mage Chains' does not exist in Xerath's kit.
audit.corrected: Channel interrupt stated in spikes[1].text, content.mid, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t; 'Mage Chains' replaced with Shocking Orb / Eye of Destruction in mid, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[0].

audit.why: It is the field that carries real numbers.
audit.corrected: Shocking Orb 13s->11s, Arcanopulse 9s, Eye of Destruction 14s, Petrifying Gaze 120s against his 130s channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad pastes; dosFull[2].d promised grounding against a champion with no dash.
audit.why: Miasma's grounding does nothing to Xerath — he has no movement ability in the kit — so the slow is the part that matters.

edits.before: Cassiopeia's ability to close distance and punish mana-heavy poke outweighs Xerath's range advantage
edits.after: Xerath's Arcanopulse outranges every tool she has, so level 1 is free poke he never pays for

edits.before: Cassiopeia continues to threaten trades whenever Xerath oversteps, keeping the lane in her favor
edits.after: Eye of Destruction slows her out of fang range while he keeps poking from a thousand units

edits.before: Cassiopeia's damage and all-in potential dominate once Xerath's poke pattern becomes predictable
edits.after: Shocking Orb comes online and any stun he lands turns a poke exchange into half her health

edits.before: Cassiopeia holds a clear lead heading into 6 thanks to superior close-range trading power
edits.after: Xerath's mana passive keeps him poking while she has to ration Noxious Blast and her fangs

edits.before: Cassiopeia's Petrifying Gaze punishes Xerath's total lack of mobility whenever she closes the gap
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane hits from 5000 range, so he threatens her health bar without ever being in hers

edits.before: Cassiopeia's item-fueled poke and burst outclass Xerath's ranged damage at closer engagement ranges
edits.after: Her first item closes the damage gap, but Xerath still chooses the range every exchange happens at

edits.before: Cassiopeia's gap-close tools and DoT stacking guarantee kills whenever Xerath is caught without support
edits.after: She wins any fight she actually reaches, and with peel in front of him she rarely gets to reach one

edits.before: Q poke on his last-hits — the poison-into-E pattern starts at level 1 and your DPS already out-trades most mids.
edits.after: Arcanopulse reaches 750 and your fangs only 700 — he pokes your last-hits for free and you cannot answer at level 1.

edits.before: W changes the geometry: miasma GROUNDS dashes. Drop it on his engage path and the lane's mobility advantage evaporates.
edits.after: Eye of Destruction lands from 1000 range and slows you inside it — Miasma grounds dashes he does not have, so it saves nothing.

edits.before: Full kit: Q-poison into spammable E twin fangs is real sustained damage. Trade anyone who steps into Q range.
edits.after: Shocking Orb online at 1050 range: one stun and the Q behind it takes a third of you before you reach 700.

edits.before: Tear stacking quietly while your E heals off poisoned targets — you win every extended trade from here.
edits.after: His Q drops to 6s while yours is 3.5s, but he casts from further — stack Tear and take the safe farm.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze online — the all-in answer. Face-stun his engage or slow his retreat; either way the fangs finish it.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane fires from 5000 range, so he chunks you from off-screen; your R only answers if you are within 825.

edits.before: Seraph's/Liandry's spike: your DPS is now the highest in the lane, melee-DPS-carry high. Force extended trades on every cooldown gap.
edits.after: Seraph's closes the damage gap, but Xerath still picks the range — until you force a fight inside 700, the poke war stays his.

edits.before: Late-game Cass is a hyper-carry: ground their divers, petrify their engage, and machine-gun whoever is closest.
edits.after: Two items in you are the better fighter, yet he never has to fight — with a peel support he pokes from 1000 all game.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb from 1050 and following with Arcanopulse before you ever reach your own 700 range.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. It governs your forward steps. - R Petrifying Gaze spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 and 11s at rank 5, and it is his only CC — dodge it and the artillery never converts. - Arcanopulse is 9s at rank 1, Eye of Destruction 14s. - Petrifying Gaze is 120s and cancels his 130s channel; that is the trade worth making.

edits.before: Carry by DPS — no mid matches your damage-per-second from two items; your job is staying alive long enough to prove it.
edits.after: Carry by arrival: your damage beats his the moment you are inside 700, so every item slot should buy the survival to get there.

edits.before: Ahead, suffocate: poison every last-hit, zone Xerath off the wave with fang threat, and call your jungler — your W makes every gank a guaranteed kill.
edits.after: Ahead, suffocate: poison every last-hit and hold the wave near your side — Xerath has no dash, so a jungler arriving onto your Miasma slow is a kill.

edits.before: Q the last-hit window, E-E-E while the poison ticks, and walk back as it fades — three fangs and out, repeat until Xerath is executable.
edits.after: Noxious Blast first — Twin Fang only hits hard on a poisoned target, costs 40 mana on a 0.75s cooldown, and you get three off per Blast.

edits.before: Xerath spends Shocking Orb (Stun) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Miasma's slow, not its grounding, is what matters here — Xerath has no dash to ground.

edits.before: That is Xerath’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Standing at 1000 range is free damage for Eye of Destruction.

edits.before: Spamming unpoisoned fangs at full mana cost, or holding W so long the dash you were saving it for already happened.
edits.after: Unpoisoned Twin Fang costs the same 40 mana for a fraction of the damage — no Blast, no E, or you lose the mana war outright.

edits.before: Track Xerath’s Shocking Orb (Stun): His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Shocking Orb (13s at rank 1): it is his only CC, and without it the artillery never converts. Petrifying Gaze also cancels his R channel.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane doesn't threaten your HP total much on its own, and your Petrifying Gaze lets you close the gap and punish him the instant he over-commits or misses a root.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane is a channel — Petrifying Gaze interrupts it and strands him on a 130-second ultimate, so hold R for his cast rather than spending it to open a trade.

edits.before: Once you hit 6, Xerath's ultimate hits from absurd range but doesn't stop you from closing the gap with Ghost, flash-engage, or simply walking up during minion cover. Petrifying Gaze locks him down completely if you get in range, since he has zero movement tools to escape a stun — punish every over-extension or missed Mage Chains root.
edits.after: Once you hit 6, Rite of the Arcane is a channel — Petrifying Gaze from 825 cancels it outright and wastes a 130-second ultimate. He has zero movement tools, so a stun that lands ends him; the whole problem is arriving, so walk up under minion cover and punish every missed Shocking Orb, which is down 13 seconds at rank 1.

edits.before: Look for all-in windows whenever Xerath oversteps or misses Mage Chains
edits.after: Look for all-in windows whenever Xerath oversteps or misses Shocking Orb

edits.before: Poke from max range with Arcanopulse and Mage Chains without ever engaging
edits.after: Poke from max range with Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction, never engaging

notes: This matchup had the cross-layer disagreement on all seven rows: content win[N] said Cassiopeia, full phases[N].side said Xerath, and packet.defects flagged the content chart against a 46.59% win rate. I moved the content layer to Xerath (matching the sides already on disk, the win rate, and the HARD 8/10 rating) rather than the other way, and rewrote all seven full-layer whys, which were the generic Cassiopeia template sitting under Xerath sides. No phases[N].side edit was needed since they already read Xerath. 'Mage Chains' is a fabricated name for Xerath's E (Shocking Orb) and appeared in three content fields — all three fixed. Xerath has no dash anywhere in his kit, so any page copy selling Miasma's grounding against him is dead advice; I rewrote dosFull[2].d but dontsFull[1].d still leans on 'the next engage arrives ungrounded' and I left it rather than invent a replacement.
